question: What is the oxidation state of chromium in chromate and dichromate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**+6**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Oxygen's oxidation state: **In most compounds, oxygen has an oxidation state of -2. This is a standard rule of oxidation states.
 
• **Chromium's oxidation state in Chromate (CrO₄²⁻):**
 
• Each chromate ion contains one chromium atom and four oxygen atoms.
 
• If we assign each oxygen an oxidation state of -2, the total contribution of the oxygen atoms to the oxidation state of the ion is -2 × 4 = -8.
 
• The ion as a whole has a charge of -2, so the** chromium must have an oxidation state of +6 **to balance out the -8 from the oxygen atoms.
 
• **Chromium's oxidation state in Dichromate (Cr₂O₇²⁻):**
 
• Each dichromate ion contains two chromium atoms and seven oxygen atoms.
 
• If we assign each oxygen an oxidation state of -2, the total contribution of the oxygen atoms to the oxidation state of the ion is -2 × 7 = -14.
 
• The ion as a whole has a charge of -2, so the total oxidation state of the two chromium atoms must be +12 (to balance out the -14 from the oxygen atoms).
 
• Since there are two chromium atoms, **each must have an oxidation state of +12/2 = +6.**
